summary: Poractant alfa (Curosurf) is a natural porcine-derived pulmonary surfactant indicated for the rescue treatment of respiratory distress syndrome (RDS) in premature infants, where it reduces mortality and pneumothoraces. It is administered intratracheally only, by or under the supervision of clinicians experienced in neonatal intubation and ventilation. The initial dose is 2.5 mL/kg (200 mg/kg) of birth weight, with up to two repeat doses of 1.25 mL/kg about 12 hours apart (maximum total 5 mL/kg). Administration can rapidly improve oxygenation and lung compliance, so ventilatory support must be adjusted promptly. Transient administration-related events include bradycardia, hypotension, oxygen desaturation, and endotracheal tube blockage, which require pausing dosing and corrective measures.
indications: Rescue treatment of Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS) in premature infants (reduces mortality and pneumothoraces associated with RDS)

admin: For intratracheal administration only, by clinicians experienced in intubation, ventilator management, and neonatal care
Confirm proper placement and patency of the endotracheal tube before dosing
Warm the vial and gently turn it to resuspend; do not shake; do not filter; do not warm and return to refrigerator
Administer in divided aliquots through a 5 French end-hole catheter with repositioning, or as a single bolus through the secondary lumen of a dual-lumen ETT without interrupting ventilation
Maintain SaO2 >92% with supplemental oxygen before dosing and adjust ventilator settings rapidly as compliance/oxygenation change
moa: Endogenous pulmonary surfactant lowers surface tension at the alveolar air-liquid interface and stabilizes alveoli against collapse at resting transpulmonary pressures. Premature infants deficient in surfactant develop RDS with poor lung expansion, inadequate gas exchange, and atelectasis. Poractant alfa, a natural porcine surfactant containing phospholipids (chiefly phosphatidylcholine/dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine) and hydrophobic surfactant proteins SP-B and SP-C, replaces the deficient surfactant and restores surface activity to the lungs.

preg: Not applicable. Poractant alfa is administered intratracheally to premature neonates with RDS, not to pregnant patients; there is no maternal-use indication.
lact: Not applicable. The product is administered directly to the neonate; it is not relevant to maternal lactation.
renal: Not applicable. Poractant alfa acts locally within the lung after intratracheal administration; no human pharmacokinetic (absorption/elimination) studies have been performed and no renal dosing considerations apply.
hepatic: Not applicable. The drug acts locally in the lung and is not characterized by systemic hepatic metabolism; no hepatic dosing considerations apply.

counsel: This medicine is given by the neonatal care team directly into your baby's breathing tube to help the lungs work
Your baby will be closely monitored on a ventilator with continuous oxygen and heart-rate monitoring
Settings on the breathing machine may change quickly as the lungs improve
Ask the team about your baby's progress and the reasons for any repeat doses
This is a specialist hospital treatment - no home administration is involved

pearls: Surfactant replacement for neonatal RDS (rescue) - reduces mortality and pneumothoraces; given INTRATRACHEALLY only
Initial dose 2.5 mL/kg (200 mg/kg) birth weight; up to two repeats of 1.25 mL/kg ~12 h apart; max total 5 mL/kg
Transient administration-related bradycardia, hypotension, desaturation, and ETT blockage are common - pause dosing and stabilize, then resume
Oxygenation and compliance can improve rapidly - reduce ventilator/oxygen settings promptly to avoid hyperoxia/overdistension
This monograph is based on the FDA insert for Curosurf (a porcine biologic surfactant); must be given by clinicians experienced in neonatal intensive care
missed: Not applicable in the usual sense. Repeat doses are given on a clinician-determined schedule (about every 12 hours) only if the infant remains intubated and meets criteria; there is no patient self-administered schedule.
overdose: There have been no reports of overdose with poractant alfa. In the event of accidental overdosage with clear effects on respiration, ventilation, or oxygenation, aspirate as much of the suspension as possible and provide supportive treatment, with particular attention to fluid and electrolyte balance.
